title: Dismantling what no longer convinces
meaning: You can revise an unsound decision when the wish to clear its foundation preserves respect for principles you both share.
text: Shared will sometimes appears through refusing to continue something built on a mistaken assumption. The Tower in the physical position of Manipura describes dismantling an unsound arrangement: cancelling a flawed procedure, removing an obstacle and admitting that the earlier scheme fails. The Tower in energy identifies the motive, wanting freedom from a foundation you can no longer defend. The Hierophant in emotions allows trust to be sought in shared principles. One appearance concerns action, the other its reason, while an accepted principle helps you experience the loss of a familiar form.

For example, you discover that your household task list repeatedly counts some jobs while overlooking others. You decide to replace it. **Dismantling a failed arrangement is easier when you know what you preserve.** Beyond the old list, a principle of participation by both remains. That can support revising responsibilities even if the original table produced more arguments than useful guidance.

The difficulty is declaring every previous agreement invalid alongside the faulty scheme. Clearing space then becomes a dispute about whose rules deserve respect at all. You seek support in an increasingly strict norm while the practical question remains unanswered. Common principles help when they allow a fresh agreement, rather than forbidding you to acknowledge a mistake in something you once accepted together.
